evidence.raw:
Multiparametric MRI Prostate | 15 January 2025 | Amsterdam UMC, AMC

Clinical context: Ascending PSA (5.2 ng/mL) alongside a previously documented positive biopsy bucket. Prior imaging carried a PI-RADS 4 designation.

FINDINGS: Prostate volume registers at 34.49 mL. A discrete hypointense focus occupies the right anterior mid-gland, spanning roughly 12 x 9 x 10 mm on T2-weighted sequences. DWI shows pronounced restricted diffusion paired with notably low ADC values. Early focal enhancement characterizes the DCE sequences. The peripheral zone remains clear. Extraprostatic extension and seminal vesicle invasion are absent. Pelvic lymphadenopathy is not present.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 4 lesion in the right anterior mid-gland. Prostate volume 34.49 mL. PSAD 0.151 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.5618297.

Multiparametric MRI Prostate | 05 Jan 2025 | Radiology Division

Clinical context: Assessment undertaken due to a previous prostate cancer diagnosis. Presenting PSA measures 6.8 ng/mL, classified as PI-RADS 4.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 36.0 mL in overall volume. T2-weighted sequences capture a localized hypointense area within the left peripheral zone, situated at the base-to-mid transition. This focus spans roughly 12 mm at its widest point. Diffusion-weighted imaging displays intense restriction, mirrored by diminished signal intensity on the apparent diffusion coefficient map. Following contrast administration, dynamic sequences highlight an early, focal enhancement pattern distinct from adjacent tissue. Extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle infiltration are absent. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal, and skeletal structures show no metastatic deposits.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone. Prostate volume 36.0 mL, PSA density 0.2 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.82952833.

Multiparametric MRI Prostate | 05 Jan 2025 | Radiology Division

Clinical context: Assessment undertaken due to a previous prostate cancer diagnosis. Presenting PSA measures 6.8 ng/mL, classified as PI-RADS 4.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 36.0 mL in overall volume. T2-weighted sequences capture a localized hypointense area within the left peripheral zone, situated at the base-to-mid transition. Following contrast administration, dynamic sequences highlight an early, focal enhancement pattern distinct from adjacent tissue. Extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle infiltration are absent. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal, and skeletal structures show no metastatic deposits.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone. Prostate volume 36.0 mL, PSA density 0.2 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.82952833.

note_sections.t: Persistent uncertainty regarding prostate cancer screening warrants re-evaluation after an earlier negative biopsy and a steady PSA course.

A 63-year-old civil engineer initially entered evaluation years ago after a mildly elevated PSA triggered a systematic biopsy that returned entirely benign. He currently experiences moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, notably nocturia twice nightly and a slightly weak stream, yielding an IPSS score of 10. Medical background includes well-controlled hypertension and hypercholesterolaemia, treated with amlodipine, lisinopril, metoprolol, and atorvastatin, plus occasional paracetamol PRN for osteoarthritis. He maintains a 36 pack-year smoking history and drinks roughly 26 units of alcohol weekly. Daily fitness routines include a 20-minute walk. Beyond urological matters, he recently finished six physiotherapy sessions for mechanical lower back pain, keeps up with regular dental check-ups, and manages mild visual impairment requiring large-print materials. He lives with his wife; their adult children visit weekly, and he continues active involvement in local engineering consultancy projects.

DRE — texture: smooth and symmetric; consistency: normal; asymmetry/nodules: absent. Vital signs reveal a blood pressure of 142/80 mmHg and a regular heart rate of 67 beats per minute. General inspection shows no peripheral oedema, while abdominal palpation confirms the absence of suprapubic tenderness or palpable masses.
